retail_comparison.title: Retail company counts fell overall, while middle receipt bands grew
retail_comparison.subtitle: Change in company counts by annual receipts, Hong Kong, 2023–2024
retail_comparison.chart: Diverging percentage-change bars, common scale -20% to +60%; all-retail reference separate
caveats: 2023–2024 retail company counts by annual receipts, C&SD Table 630-76003. Receipt bands are cross-sectional, not fixed cohorts or closure rates.

The distribution shift is an observed change in cross-sectional counts. It is consistent with multiple combinations of entry, exit and movement between receipts bands; this table alone does not identify those flows.
Nominal receipt thresholds do not identify ownership, chain affiliation, employment size, or a fixed cohort. Do not infer that locally owned shops closed or that larger chains gained.
No causal attribution to northbound spending, retail leakage, rents, tourism, inflation or any other mechanism is supported by these counts alone.
Use company terminology consistently with the current same-series table. Do not mix the older establishment-labelled PDF with these counts.

wage_guardrail.label: Accommodation and food service activities (broader than F&B)
wage_guardrail.caveat: These figures cover accommodation plus food service activities and full-time employees up to supervisory level in selected industries. Do not label them F&B-only or total earnings including overtime.

caveats: Cross-sector evidence is a contrast, not a causal estimate of labour importation.
F&B is a surveyed industry; HA is one public employer. Populations and measures differ.
The 36 nurses are new long-term starters under the newer channels, not all non-local nurses employed by HA. Exchange nurses are a distinct short-term programme.
No Shenzhen-specific daily commuter count or occupation/wage model is inferred.
Employment/vacancy percentages are official published changes from unrounded figures; retain them rather than recomputing from rounded counts.
